answer: Require one randomized key-generation ceremony on an independent hardware security module (HSM): it derives a public key from a violet/beacon/opal nonce and signs the firmware hash, slot ID and attestation chain. The registry activates only a valid chain and consumes its device serial, rejecting duplicate serials or altered firmware. Proposed HSM session fee: .30 per identity, not a live protocol rule. One honest agent pays .30 once; 1,000 fake identities cost ,300 (1,000 × .30). Limitation: HSM access is uneven and providers can collude.
